title: Speaking quietly, touch, music, and presence when someone seems less aware

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A person near death no longer answers, seems asleep or unresponsive, and the room shifts toward voice, touch, music, ordinary presence, and the question of whether the person can still hear.
ordinary_language_queries: can she hear me when she is dying
what should I say if he cannot respond
should I talk to someone unconscious at end of life

content_layers.observation_text: Public family-facing sources commonly tell witnesses that hearing may remain possible when a dying person seems sleepy or unresponsive, and suggest calm presence, speech, touch, or music if wanted.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK, Marie Curie, and healthdirect all support a cautious presence record: speak normally, avoid assuming the person cannot hear, and preserve family/cultural preferences.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This is the first practice record that treats presence itself as a care move. It gives the corpus a way to collect how people inhabit the room without pretending to know what the dying person hears.

what_this_is_not: not proof the person hears or understands every word
not an instruction to touch if touch was not wanted
not a script for forgiveness or goodbye
not a spiritual claim about awareness
uncertainties: The person’s interior experience is usually unknown.
Touch, music, prayer, and speech may be welcome, unwanted, culturally specific, or relationship-dependent.
Future consented records should preserve exactly what families and practitioners said, not just that they spoke.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should permit ordinary speech and silence without making either obligatory. It should remove the fear that there is one correct sentence.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect room-language craft: how to invite speech, how to protect quiet, how to ask about touch or music, and how to avoid coercive goodbye rituals.
language_notes: Prefer “may still be able to hear” over certainty.
Record the sounds of the room without sentimentality.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
